newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: BAD WEATHER CUTS CZECH BEET YIELD FCASTS.
newsitem.headline: BAD WEATHER CUTS CZECH BEET YIELD FCASTS.

text.p: Continuing rainy weather is hampering the Czech sugar beet harvest and earlier yield estimates are proving too optimistic, Jiri Janda, the director of sugar refiner Prazska Cukerni Spolecnost, said on Monday.
Janda said that bad weather continuing in September caused a lower-than-expected sugar content, but added that domestic demand for sugar would be covered from this year's campaign.

In the late summer industry experts were optimistic about this year's campaign, saying refined sugar production would exceed 500,000 tonnes after 460,035 tonnes last year, but Janda told Reuters it was not clear now what the figure would be.
"It is difficult to say now what the definitive result will be, but the sugar content is not as high as expected.
"It was expected that there would be some warmer weather in September which did not come, there was minimum sunshine. That reduced the (sugar content and yield) forecasts," said Janda.
Beet yield per hectare was likely to be slightly above last year's figures, but lower than the "extreme high" of earlier forecasts. He declined to make a firm yield forecast.

The Czech Statistical Bureau said in August that it expected a harvest of 4.221 million tonnes this year, after 3.712 million in 1995, with yield of beet per hectare rising to 40.55 tonnes from 39.86 tonnes last year.

Janda said that wet conditions hampered the start of the harvest the week before last. "The weather was adverse in the first week, it was raining, conditions were very difficult for harvesting... now it is getting better," he said.

"The contamination (with mud) is high, it ranges around up to 20 percent. If the (wet) weather continues further, the harvest will be extremely difficult, losses on fields will rise and the final result will be much lower than originally expected," he warned.
